gmail.read_attachment.name: gmail.read_attachment
gmail.read_attachment.title: read_attachment
gmail.read_attachment.description: Read one attachment from a Gmail message. First read/search the parent message and select an entry from its attachments, inline_images, or API-content MIME parts. For an attachments entry or downloadable MIME part, call this action only when its read_attachment_supported field is true; when false, do not call this action because the MIME type is unsupported. Pass the parent message id as message_id. Prefer the entry's non-null attachment_id or MIME part's body.attachment_id when its complete value is available; when it is absent or marked truncated, pass the exact filename instead. Do not synthesize attachment IDs from filenames, content IDs, x-attachment IDs, URLs, or user text. The original attachment is returned as file_uri. Small extracted content and images are included inline. If content_truncated is true, the inline text is only a preview; read extraction_file_uri for the complete extracted content and images as JSON.

message_id.description: Gmail message ID returned by Gmail search/read results. Use the `id` or `message_id` field from an email result. Do not pass placeholder values like `dummy`, `latest`, `gmail:<id>`, draft IDs, thread IDs, email addresses, subjects, or Gmail UI URLs. Use the parent message ID.
message_id.title: Message Id

filename.description: Exact attachment filename from the parent message's attachments, inline_images, or API-content MIME parts. Use only when attachment_id is absent, unknown, or marked truncated in the tool response. If multiple attachments share this filename, retry with a complete attachment_id.
filename.title: Filename

attachment_id.description: Exact Gmail attachment_id copied from the selected attachment's attachments[].attachment_id or inline_images[].attachment_id, or from a downloadable API-content MIME part's body.attachment_id. Use it only when the complete value is available; if it is absent or marked truncated in a tool response, pass the exact filename instead. Do not pass truncated values, filenames, message IDs, thread IDs, Content-ID, X-Attachment-Id, URLs, or guessed values.
attachment_id.title: Attachment Id

_meta.connector_description: Gmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions.

(Beta) Returns native and inferred projects, owned goals, and focus areas for up to 10 root identifiers per call, including their immediate reports by default. Includes project ownership and contribution relationships, status, and updates.

This tool is in beta and is not generally available. Usage is not billed during beta. Pricing details will be announced when the tool becomes generally available.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. identifiers.description: Select 1–10 roots by account ID or IdentityUser ARI, returning a batch with one portfolio per root, including for a single entry. Each also includes its immediate reports by default; do not add those reports as roots again. Use includeDirectReports=false for a flat batch. Cannot combine with name or email.

name.description: Resolve one person by name. If multiple people match, use the returned candidates to identify the intended person; ask the user if unclear, then retry with email set to the candidate's exact email, or identifiers set to [candidate.accountId]. Omit name from the retry request.

email.description: Resolve one person by exact email.

includeDirectReports.description: true returns the root AND each immediate report’s work in this call. false returns only the selected root(s). Never includes grandchildren for a single root.

kinds.description: Nonempty subset of projects, goals, focusAreas. Default: all three.

projectRoles.description: Project relationships: owner and/or contributor. Default: both. Goals and focus areas are owned.

includeInferredProjects.description: Include active inferred projects with their linked evidence, independently of native project filters.

atlasProjectStatus.description: Atlassian project filter; default in progress. Does not filter inferred-project health.

goalStatus.description: Omit for in-progress OR pending goals. An explicit status selects only that state; active excludes pending.

focusAreaStatus.description: Omit for in-progress OR pending focus areas. An explicit status selects only that state; active excludes pending.

includeLinks.description: Include directly linked native goals/projects with separate relationship coverage.

limitPerCollection.description: Records per person per source collection, 1–100. Atlassian and inferred projects have independent limits.

reportLimit.description: Maximum direct reports to query, 1–100; omitted reports remain explicit in coverage.

google_calendar.search.name: google_calendar.search
google_calendar.search.title: search
google_calendar.search.description: Search Google Calendar events within a time window. To obtain the full information for an event, use read_event. Accepted parameters are only `query`, `max_results`, `time_min`, `time_max`, `calendar_id`, and `next_page_token`. `query` is broad free text, not a structured search language. Prefer passing explicit `time_min` and `time_max` for every search, then page with `next_page_token` inside that bounded window before widening the query. Do not pass unsupported fields like `topn`, `timezone_str`, `user_message`, or `best_effort_fetch`.

query.description: Optional broad free-text query passed to Google Calendar's `q` search parameter. Omit to return events within the time window without a text filter. Best for keyword matches in titles and some indexed event text, not precise attendee filtering.
query.title: Query

max_results.description: Maximum number of events to return. Must be at least 1.
max_results.title: Max Results

time_min.description: Optional window start in full ISO-8601/RFC3339 format (e.g. 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z).
time_min.title: Time Min

time_max.description: Optional window end in full ISO-8601/RFC3339 format (e.g. 2026-05-31T23:59:59Z).
time_max.title: Time Max

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID to query. Use `primary` for the user's main calendar, or an ID returned by `list_calendars` for a secondary, shared, or resource calendar. Default is `primary`.
calendar_id.title: Calendar Id

next_page_token.description: Non-empty token returned by this search. Omit on the first page; keep all other arguments the same when requesting the next page.
next_page_token.title: Next Page Token

chatgpt_space.find_pages.description: Find accessible Pages matching a query, optionally within one Space. Results are bounded, not an exhaustive listing.
